question: Why does ViT matter for DINOv3’s dense features?
direct_answer: Because ViT produces patch tokens that can stay spatially meaningful, which supports dense representations.
expanded_answer: A Vision Transformer splits an image into patches and processes them as tokens. That gives DINOv3 access not only to a global image representation but also to patch-level outputs, which is important when the goal is to preserve local spatial information for dense tasks.
key_points: Patch-level outputs are available for downstream use
Fits dense tasks better than a purely global embedding
common_wrong_ideas: Thinking transformers remove all spatial structure
Assuming only the class token matters
